name: Publish

# Publishes the tagged version to the public registry.
#
# Auth is tokenless: npm Trusted Publishing mints a short-lived credential from
# the GitHub OIDC token, so no NPM_TOKEN secret exists here after the bootstrap.
# The trusted publisher is registered against THIS file's path - renaming or
# moving it breaks publishing until it is re-registered.
#
# --provenance is carried because ADR-007 makes the repository public. npm
# refuses an attestation whose source repository an unauthenticated client
# cannot resolve.
#
# The publish is staged rather than direct. The tarball, its dist-tag and its
# provenance all reach the registry, but the version is not installable until a
# maintainer approves the stage with 2FA - the package page's Versions tab, or
# `npm stage list` then `npm stage approve <id>`. Nothing this workflow can do
# makes a version installable on its own, which is the only brake there is on
# the one step here that cannot be undone.
#
# Publishing a GitHub Release is what starts this file. The release carries the
# `vX.Y.Z` tag and the notes; the version itself is the one already committed in
# `package.json`, and the guard below refuses a tag that disagrees with it - so a
# release names a version the repository agreed to in a pull request rather than
# minting one at the point of no return. Draft releases fire nothing. Editing a
# release that is already published fires this again and the second run fails at
# the registry against a version that exists, which publishes nothing.
#
# Three preconditions, all of which fail closed rather than publishing wrongly:
#   1. npm >= 11.15.0. Trusted publishing needs 11.5.1 and `npm stage` needs
#      11.15.0, and Node 22 ships an older npm, so the job installs it.
#   2. The repository is public. Until it is, --provenance fails here.
#   3. A trusted publisher exists for this name. It cannot, before the first
#      publish: npm has nothing to attach one to. The first release therefore
#      carries a token, by hand, and every release after it is tokenless. That
#      token is revoked immediately afterwards.

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  # The way back in when a publish fails after the release already exists.
  # Select the release's tag, not a branch: the version guard below refuses
  # anything that is not a vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH tag, so a branch fails closed.
  workflow_dispatch:

# Least privilege by default: only the publish job opts into id-token: write,
# and it does not start until every gate below has passed.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # The gates that speak to the artefact, re-run against the tagged commit:
  # type check, lint, format, tests, build, doc blocks and the tarball itself.
  # The gates that speak only to the repository - spec anchors, spike status,
  # regions, citation names - stay on ci.yml. A tag points at whatever its
  # author chose, so passing on main is not evidence about what is published.
  verify:
    name: Verify the release candidate
    # Refused before a runner starts, as well as by the version guard: nothing
    # here passes --tag, so a prerelease would reach the registry as `latest`.
    if: ${{ !github.event.release.prerelease }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Ancestry needs the graph connecting the tag to main; a release
          # event checks out one commit by default.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install (no build)
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # main is the trust boundary: it requires a pull request, blocks
      # force-pushes, and publishing over OIDC makes push access to it the right
      # to release. A release can be cut against any branch or commit, so
      # without this the boundary is bypassable by whoever can draft one. Not repeated in the
      # publish job below - `needs` carries it, and ancestry once true stays
      # true while force-pushes to main are blocked.
      # No fetch here either, for the reason ci.yml's changelog step carries:
      # the checkout's credential does not outlive it. Publishing from a public
      # repository would have let an anonymous fetch succeed and hidden that.
      - name: Tagged commit is on main
        run: |
          if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "${GITHUB_SHA}" origin/main; then
            echo "publish: FAILED - ${GITHUB_SHA} is not an ancestor of origin/main" >&2
            echo "publish: cut the release from a commit merged to main" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "publish: tagged commit is on main"

      - name: Tag matches the committed version
        run: npm run check:version

      # The pre-commit sequence AGENTS.md documents, re-run against the tagged
      # commit. Not redundant with CI: a tag points at whatever commit its author
      # chose, so a green run on main is evidence about main rather than about
      # what is being published. Separate steps so a red release names its gate.
      - name: Type check
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Type check the example
        run: npm run typecheck:example

      - name: Lint (--max-warnings 0)
        run: npm run eslint

      - name: Format check
        run: npm run prettier:check

      # The gate that catches a README or guide code block drifting from the source being published,
      # which is the one thing npm renders and the one thing a tarball cannot be re-cut to fix.
      - name: Documented code blocks
        run: npm run docs:check

      - name: Test (with coverage floor)
        run: npm run test:coverage

      - name: Build chain
        run: npm run check:build-chain

      # Explicit, before the pack: `npm pack` runs `prepare`, so without this a broken build
      # surfaces as a confusing pack failure inside the smoke script rather than as a named step.
      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Smoke (packed tarball)
        run: npm run smoke

      # reach the tarball - but the pack list is the only place that is a fact
      # rather than an intention. npm pack runs `prepare`, so this lists what
      # this commit would actually ship.
      #
      # Maps are rejected on the same grounds: with only dist/ published, a map
      # names a ../src/*.ts nobody receives.
      #
      # It asserts what MUST be there as well as what must not: a pure absence
      # check calls an empty dist/ clean and publishes a package with no entry
      # point, which is unpublishable for 72 hours and permanent after that.
      - name: Pack list carries the package and nothing else
        run: |
          npm pack --dry-run --json > pack.json
          node --input-type=module -e '
            import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
            const files = JSON.parse(readFileSync("pack.json", "utf8"))[0].files.map((f) => f.path);
            const unwanted = files.filter((p) => /(^|\/)[^/]*\.test\.[^/]*$/.test(p) || p.endsWith(".map"));
            const required = ["package.json", "README.md", "LICENSE", "dist/index.js", "dist/index.d.ts"];
            const missing = required.filter((p) => !files.includes(p));
            const unpublished = files.filter((p) => /^(src|example|smoke|docs|specs|adrs|scripts)\//.test(p));
            const { filename, name, version } = JSON.parse(readFileSync("pack.json", "utf8"))[0];
            const expected = name.replace("@", "").replace("/", "-") + "-" + version + ".tgz";
            if (unwanted.length > 0) {
              console.error("pack list carries test files or source maps:\n  " + unwanted.join("\n  "));
              process.exit(1);
            }
            if (missing.length > 0) {
              console.error("pack list is missing:\n  " + missing.join("\n  "));
              process.exit(1);
            }
            if (unpublished.length > 0) {
              console.error("pack list carries trees that files:[\"dist\"] excludes:\n  " + unpublished.join("\n  "));
              process.exit(1);
            }
            if (filename !== expected) {
              console.error(`tarball is named ${filename}, expected ${expected}`);
              process.exit(1);
            }
            console.log(`pack list clean: ${files.length} files as ${filename}, entry point present, dist/ only`);
          '

  publish:
    name: Publish to npm
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write # npm OIDC trusted publishing
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

      # Trusted publishing needs npm >= 11.5.1, `npm stage` needs >= 11.15.0, and Node 22 ships an
      # older npm. Pinned to the 11.x line rather than `latest`: this is the one job holding
      # id-token: write, and `latest` lets a major nobody here has run decide how the publish behaves.
      - name: Upgrade npm for OIDC trusted publishing and staging
        run: npm install -g npm@^11.15.0

      - name: Install (no build)
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # Repeated from `verify` deliberately: it is the last gate before the one
      # step in this repository that cannot be undone.
      - name: Tag matches the committed version
        run: npm run check:version

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      # --ignore-scripts so `prepare` does not rebuild: what ships is the tree
      # the step above produced, not a second build of it. pipefail so a failed
      # stage is not masked by the tee that feeds the job summary.
      - name: Stage the version on npm
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          npm stage publish --access public --provenance --ignore-scripts 2>&1 | tee stage.log
          {
            echo "## Staged - a maintainer must approve it before anyone can install it"
            echo
            echo "The package page's Versions tab -> Approve, with 2FA. Or: \`npm stage list\`, then \`npm stage approve <id>\`."
            echo
            echo '```'
            cat stage.log
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

# npm with provenance, and tag the Go module packages/agent-contracts-go at the same
# version. The TS types are regenerated from the D model first and the

# Auth is tokenless via npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC): no NPM_TOKEN secret. It needs
# `id-token: write` (below), npm >= 11.5.1 (upgraded below), and a trusted publisher
# configured for @re-cinq/agent-contracts on npmjs.com pointing at this repo and the
# publish-contracts.yml workflow. The package's first-ever publish must be done once
# with a token before the trusted publisher can be registered on npmjs.com.

on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write # npm provenance via the GitHub OIDC token

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
      - uses: dlang-community/setup-dlang@d7d85fcde7c4cd5f9a6618fce1bccc316e1e910b # v2
        with:
          compiler: dmd-2.111.0
      - name: Contracts drift check (types match the D model)
        run: ./scripts/check-contracts-drift.sh
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
      - name: Upgrade npm for OIDC trusted publishing
        run: npm install -g npm@^11.5.1
      # A tag whose package.json was never bumped republishes an existing version,
      # which npm rejects — and the rejection reads like an auth failure, so it went
      # unnoticed from v0.5.0 to v0.7.0 (#139). Fail here instead, naming the bump.
      - name: Package version matches the release tag
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        env:
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: ./scripts/check-contracts-version.sh "$TAG"
      - name: Install, test (100% coverage gate), build
        working-directory: packages/agent-contracts
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run test:coverage
          npm run build
      - name: Publish to npm
        working-directory: packages/agent-contracts
        run: npm publish --provenance --access public

  # Go modules publish through git tags: a module in a subdirectory is versioned by a
  # tag prefixed with its path. Tagging the release commit makes
  # `go get github.com/re-cinq/ai-agent-subsystem/packages/agent-contracts-go@vX.Y.Z` resolve.
  publish-go:
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write # push the module tag
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
      - uses: dlang-community/setup-dlang@d7d85fcde7c4cd5f9a6618fce1bccc316e1e910b # v2
        with:
          compiler: dmd-2.111.0
      - name: Contracts drift check (types match the D model)
        run: ./scripts/check-contracts-drift.sh
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version-file: packages/agent-contracts-go/go.mod
          cache-dependency-path: packages/agent-contracts-go/go.sum
      - name: Vet, gofmt and test
        run: make contracts-go
      - name: Tag the Go module
        env:
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          git tag "packages/agent-contracts-go/$TAG" "$GITHUB_SHA"
          git push origin "packages/agent-contracts-go/$TAG"

    if: ${{ !github.event.release.prerelease }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      # tag can point at anything, and this is the last gate before the
      # package is public and immutable. Cheap insurance against an
      # unversioned republish.

      - name: Typecheck

      # dangerous scheme in the default allowlist blocks the release.

      - name: Test (coverage gate)

## Releases

A release is two acts by a maintainer: publish a GitHub Release, then approve the version npm
has staged. Nothing is bumped, tagged or published by hand, and no pull request is needed for a
version to exist.

1. Releases → **Draft a new release** → _Choose a tag_ → type `vX.Y.Z` → _Create new tag on
   publish_. Patch for fixes, minor for features; 1.0 is a decision, not a side effect.
2. Target `main`, title `vX.Y.Z`, **Generate release notes** (the merged pull requests since the
   previous tag become the notes - keep pull-request titles honest for that reason).
3. Leave _pre-release_ unticked; the workflow refuses pre-releases. **Publish release**.
4. When the `Publish` workflow run is green, approve the staged version: npmjs.com → the
   package page → **Versions** tab → the staged version → **Approve** (2FA is asked for). Or
   from a logged-in terminal with npm 11.15 or newer (`npx -y npm@11 ...` if yours is older):
   `npm stage list @re-cinq/bowman-ui`, then `npm stage approve <id>`; the id is also in the
   workflow run's job summary. Until then the version is on the registry with its provenance
   but not installable, and `npm stage download <id>` hands you the exact tarball to inspect
   first.

The `published` event runs `.github/workflows/publish.yml`: the `verify` job re-runs every gate
at the tag; the `publish` job stamps the tag's version into `package.json`
(`scripts/set-version-from-tag.sh` - on `main` the field is the placeholder
`0.0.0` and is never edited), builds, and runs
`npm stage publish --access public --provenance` over OIDC trusted publishing - staged, because
the trusted publisher deliberately allows no direct `npm publish`: nothing CI does on its own can
make a version installable. npm is the source of truth for versions, and
`npm view @re-cinq/bowman-ui versions` lists them. A tag that repeats a published version fails
at the registry; a failed run on an existing tag is re-run from the Actions tab (`publish.yml` →
_Run workflow_ → the tag). The assistive-technology pass in
[docs/accessibility/README.md](./docs/accessibility/README.md) is a procedure, not a release
gate: run it when you can, commit the record through a pull request, and CI validates its shape.

## Releases

Cut a release by bumping the npm package to the version you are about to tag, then pushing the tag:

```sh
(cd packages/agent-contracts && npm version 0.11.0 --no-git-tag-version)  # in the release PR
git tag v0.11.0 && git push origin v0.11.0
```

publish if the two disagree, rather than letting npm reject a duplicate version quietly.

controller and agent images for the tag (each with an SPDX SBOM and SLSA provenance attestation). It
then renders `deploy/` to a single digest-pinned `install.yaml` and attaches it to the GitHub

# Fails when a release tag and the committed package.json version disagree.

# Usage:

# version shipped under a heading that never named it.

repo="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
tag="${1:-${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}}"
version="$(node -p "require('$repo/package.json').version")"

if [ -z "$tag" ]; then
  echo "check-version: no tag given and GITHUB_REF_NAME is unset" >&2
  echo "check-version: package.json is at $version, so the tag to push is v$version" >&2
  exit 2
fi

# The workflow's `v*` filter accepts far more than a release tag does.
if ! printf '%s' "$tag" | grep -Eq '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'; then
  echo "check-version: FAILED - '$tag' is not a vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH release tag" >&2

  # every plain `npm install` would resolve to it.
  echo "check-version: prerelease tags are rejected because no dist-tag is set" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$tag" != "v$version" ]; then
  echo "check-version: FAILED - tag '$tag' and package.json '$version' disagree" >&2
  echo "check-version: bump package.json to ${tag#v}, or tag v$version instead" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Keep a Changelog writes the released version as a `## [x.y.z]` heading, optionally dated.
if ! grep -Eq "^## \\[${version//./\\.}\\]" "$repo/CHANGELOG.md"; then
  echo "check-version: FAILED - CHANGELOG.md has no '## [$version]' heading" >&2
  echo "check-version: rename '## [Unreleased]' to '## [$version]' and open a fresh one above it" >&2
  exit 1
fi

- It runs from CI rather than a laptop, so the provenance attestation is produced from the GitHub OIDC token and `0.2.0` is not permanently unattested.
- The token has to bypass two-factor authentication - `npm token create --bypass-2fa`, or the equivalent checkbox. Staging is what exists to defer proof-of-presence, and staging cannot create the package, so for this one publish the two mechanisms that would each solve it rule each other out. Presence is proven once, when the token is created.

A tag with no release still renders at `/releases/tag/v0.2.0`, which is what the changelog links to, and the publish workflow no longer triggers on a tag push - so the link resolves and nothing runs. Creating a release instead would fire `publish.yml`, pass every gate against the tagged commit and fail at the staging step against a version that already exists: a permanently red run in the history, bought for a row on the releases page. This replaces the earlier plan to accept that red run, which predates the release-event trigger. The attestation on `0.2.0` names the bootstrap workflow, which no longer exists in the tree, and `npm audit signatures` still verifies it, because the attestation records the workflow at the commit it ran from.
- Everything here happens once and cannot be redone: a published version cannot be replaced, and after 72 hours cannot be withdrawn. From `0.2.1` staging moves the point of no return from the release to the approval; for `0.2.0` it stays at the dispatch, which is why that workflow runs the full gate sequence rather than trusting the run CI did on the same commit. It therefore runs last, after the tarball smoke test passes and after the README that becomes the package's front page is correct.

name: Publish

# Publishes the tagged version to the public registry.
#
# Auth is tokenless: npm Trusted Publishing mints a short-lived credential from
# the GitHub OIDC token, so no NPM_TOKEN secret exists here after the bootstrap.
# The trusted publisher is registered against THIS file's path - renaming or
# moving it breaks publishing until it is re-registered.
#
# --provenance is carried because ADR-007 makes the repository public. npm
# refuses an attestation whose source repository an unauthenticated client
# cannot resolve.
#
# The publish is staged rather than direct. The tarball, its dist-tag and its
# provenance all reach the registry, but the version is not installable until a
# maintainer approves the stage with 2FA - the package page's Versions tab, or
# `npm stage list` then `npm stage approve <id>`. Nothing this workflow can do
# makes a version installable on its own, which is the only brake there is on
# the one step here that cannot be undone.
#
# Publishing a GitHub Release is what starts this file. The release carries the
# `vX.Y.Z` tag and the notes; the version itself is the one already committed in
# `package.json`, and the guard below refuses a tag that disagrees with it - so a
# release names a version the repository agreed to in a pull request rather than
# minting one at the point of no return. Draft releases fire nothing. Editing a
# release that is already published fires this again and the second run fails at
# the registry against a version that exists, which publishes nothing.
#
# Three preconditions, all of which fail closed rather than publishing wrongly:
#   1. npm >= 11.15.0. Trusted publishing needs 11.5.1 and `npm stage` needs
#      11.15.0, and Node 22 ships an older npm, so the job installs it.
#   2. The repository is public. Until it is, --provenance fails here.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fails when a release tag and the committed package.json version disagree.
#
# Usage:
#   bash scripts/check-version.sh v0.2.0   # before pushing the tag
#   bash scripts/check-version.sh          # in CI, reads GITHUB_REF_NAME
#
# A committed script rather than an inline workflow step: a tag that has already
# fired a publish cannot be un-pushed, so the check has to be runnable before the
# tag exists.
#
# It also holds CHANGELOG.md to the version being tagged. check-changelog.sh only
# asks that the file was touched, so the release rename was ungated and the
# version shipped under a heading that never named it.
set -euo pipefail

repo="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
tag="${1:-${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}}"
version="$(node -p "require('$repo/package.json').version")"

if [ -z "$tag" ]; then
  echo "check-version: no tag given and GITHUB_REF_NAME is unset" >&2
  echo "check-version: package.json is at $version, so the tag to push is v$version" >&2
  exit 2
fi

# The workflow's `v*` filter accepts far more than a release tag does.
if ! printf '%s' "$tag" | grep -Eq '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'; then
  echo "check-version: FAILED - '$tag' is not a vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH release tag" >&2
  # Nothing here passes --tag, so a prerelease would publish as `latest` and
  # every plain `npm install` would resolve to it.
  echo "check-version: prerelease tags are rejected because no dist-tag is set" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$tag" != "v$version" ]; then
  echo "check-version: FAILED - tag '$tag' and package.json '$version' disagree" >&2
  echo "check-version: bump package.json to ${tag#v}, or tag v$version instead" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Keep a Changelog writes the released version as a `## [x.y.z]` heading, optionally dated.
if ! grep -Eq "^## \\[${version//./\\.}\\]" "$repo/CHANGELOG.md"; then
  echo "check-version: FAILED - CHANGELOG.md has no '## [$version]' heading" >&2
  echo "check-version: rename '## [Unreleased]' to '## [$version]' and open a fresh one above it" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "check-version: OK - $tag matches package.json $version, and CHANGELOG.md names it"

name: Publish

# When a GitHub release is published, build + test @re-cinq/bowman-ui at the
# release's tag and publish it to npm.
#
# Auth is tokenless via npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC): no NPM_TOKEN secret. It
# needs `id-token: write` (on the publish job below), npm >= 11.5.1 (upgraded
# below), and a trusted publisher configured for @re-cinq/bowman-ui on
# npmjs.com pointing at this repo and this workflow. The package's first-ever
# publish must be done once with a token before the trusted publisher can be
# registered on npmjs.com.
#
# The GitHub Release is the release: a human drafts one with a `vX.Y.Z` tag
# and publishes it, and that `published` event is the way in. The version is
# taken FROM THE TAG - package.json carries a placeholder on main and is never
# bumped by hand or by a bot - so a release is one act, not a pull request
# plus a release. workflow_dispatch exists to re-run a failed publish on an
# existing tag; on any other ref the tag check below fails, since a branch
# name is not a release tag. Draft releases never fire `published`;
# pre-releases are rejected by the job condition below, so a pre-release
# cannot reach the registry.
#
# The publish job holds the OIDC credential, so it must never run untrusted
# third-party code. The example-app checks (consumer, rsc) install dependencies
# resolved live from the public registry, so they run in the read-only `verify`
# job below; the publish job only `needs:` its green result. Keeping the
# id-token job down to version-guard, install and build denies a compromised
# transitive dependency any path to the trusted-publish token.

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:

# Least privilege by default: only the publish job opts into id-token: write.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Every gate that runs third-party or example-app code lives here, in a job
  # that never sees the publish credential. The publish job below gates on it.
  verify:
    if: ${{ !github.event.release.prerelease }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-node-install
      # A release is cut from main, which CI already gated - but a release's
      # tag can point at anything, and this is the last gate before the
      # package is public and immutable. Cheap insurance against an
      # unversioned republish.
      - name: Lint (--max-warnings 0)
        run: npm run lint
      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck
      # Issue 213: the last markdown-safety gate before an immutable publish -
      # rehype-raw, a re-enabled skipHtml, a flipped allowImages default, or a
      # dangerous scheme in the default allowlist blocks the release.
      - name: Markdown safety check
        run: npm run check:markdown-safety
      - name: Test (coverage gate)
        run: npm run test:coverage
      # Issue 82: the last executable proof before the package goes public and
      # immutable - the packed tarball from this tagged commit must render the
      # full chat screen in the standalone Vite consumer.
      - name: Install chromium for the consumer check
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Consumer app check
        run: ./scripts/consumer-app.sh
      # Issue 100: the App Router client-boundary proof against the tarball
      # built from this tagged commit - the same release-candidate gate the
      # consumer check installs. Green mode only: the --expect-failure branch
      # guards the repo's own directives and already gated this commit in CI.
      - name: RSC fixture check
        run: ./scripts/rsc-fixture.sh

  publish:
    # Gate the credentialled job on every verify gate. If any is red, the
    # id-token job never starts, so the token is never minted.
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write # npm OIDC trusted publishing
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
      # Trusted publishing needs npm >= 11.5.1; `npm stage` needs >= 11.15.0.
      - name: Upgrade npm for OIDC trusted publishing and staged publishing
        run: npm install -g npm@^11.15.0
      # The tag names the version. A malformed or prerelease tag fails here;
      # a tag that repeats a published version fails at the registry, loudly,
      # which is the right place for it.
      - name: Set the version from the release tag
        env:
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name || github.ref_name }}
        run: ./scripts/set-version-from-tag.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"
      - name: Install
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts
      # Kept even though verify also builds: jobs share no filesystem, so this
      # job builds its own dist/. `files: ["dist"]` with no prepublishOnly means
      # a future test-script edit that stops building would otherwise publish an
      # empty package silently. This is the last gate before an immutable
      # publish; the explicit build stays.
      - name: Build
        run: npm run build
      # The assistive-technology pass (docs/accessibility/README.md) is a
      # procedure, not a release gate: `check-at-pass.mjs --freshness` is run
      # by hand by whoever wants its answer, and left this job on 2026-09-09.
      # --provenance: the repository is public, so every published version
      # carries a Sigstore attestation linking it to this workflow run and
      # the release's commit. It was withheld while the repo was private
      # (npm does not attest private repositories); the repo must be public
      # before the first release runs this step.
      # Staged, not direct: the trusted publisher allows `npm stage publish`
      # only (npm's recommendation, chosen 2026-09-10). The tarball, its
      # dist-tag and its provenance all reach the registry, but the version is
      # not installable until a maintainer approves the stage with 2FA - on
      # npmjs.com (the package page's Versions tab -> Approve) or with
      # `npm stage list` then `npm stage approve <id>`. Nothing this job can do
      # makes a version installable on its own. pipefail: a failed stage must
      # not be masked by the tee that feeds the job summary.
      - name: Stage the version on npm
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          npm stage publish --access public --provenance 2>&1 | tee stage.log
          {
            echo "## Staged on npm - a maintainer must approve it before it is installable"
            echo
            echo "npmjs.com -> @re-cinq/bowman-ui -> Versions tab -> Approve (2FA), or: npm stage list, then npm stage approve <id>."
            echo
            echo '```'
            cat stage.log
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
